title: Officials who decided matters involving their former clients or partners
summary: Most of the named officials have documented prior ties to parties affected by their offices. The strongest cases: Bondi (ex-Qatar registered agent) signed the memo clearing Qatar's jet; Blanche disbanded NCET while holding $159K+ in crypto; Selig's former clients Paradigm and Willkie-represented Polymarket sit on the side of the CFTC's prediction-market fight; Navarro initiated the 1789-backed Vulcan loan; and Cerberus alumni of Deputy Secretary Feinberg run the Pentagon's OSC and BOND investment arms. Reuters single-sourced Barrack's push for his partner's TI Capital, and Mother Jones and Popular Information reported Bessent's Argentina swap aiding friend Rob Citrone. For Quintenz (never confirmed), Gould, Kratsios (whose current Scale AI holding is unverified), Patel, Boulos and Charles Kushner we found ties but no specific benefiting decision. No authority has found an ethics violation in any of these cases, and most rest on timing and relationships, not proof of influence. Bondi was fired as AG on Apr 2, 2026 and Blanche became acting AG.

sub_claims.statement: Pam Bondi was a registered agent for Qatar at Ballard Partners and later backed the legality of Trump accepting Qatar's 747.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. FARA records and fact-checks show Ballard Partners was paid $115,000 a month by Qatar's embassy (about July 2019 to June 2020), with Bondi listed as key personnel. She left in Nov 2019 for Trump's impeachment defence and rejoined in Mar 2020. Her personal share is not on record, and the fact-check rates 'she personally earned $115K/month' undetermined. In May 2025 multiple outlets reported a DOJ memo, drafted by the Office of Legal Counsel and signed by Bondi (with White House counsel David Warrington), finding it 'legally permissible' to accept the jet and later transfer it to the library foundation. A DOJ official told CNN that career ethics officials found no conflict requiring recusal. CREW and Sen. Durbin argued she should have recused. The memo has not been released; Freedom of the Press Foundation sued for it after DOJ quoted a 600+ day FOIA wait. This shows a former paid foreign-agent relationship and a later decision favourable to that principal. It does not show that the lobbying shaped the memo. Bondi was fired as AG on Apr 2, 2026 (see sub-claim on her TMTG sale).

sub_claims.statement: DOJ dropped cases against clients of Bondi's brother, Brad Bondi (Paul Hastings).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the dismissals; unverified for any role by the AG. Bloomberg Law and ABC reported that DOJ dismissed charges against former Florida legislator Carolina Amesty (Aug 2025) and dropped a wire-fraud indictment of two St. Louis developers soon after they retained Brad Bondi in July 2025. Democrats (Rep. Dave Min; Sen. Schiff and others; a Mar 11, 2026 letter to the acting DOJ IG) also cite the Mar 2025 pardon of Trevor Milton, for whom Brad Bondi was lead trial counsel (see C36/C49). DOJ says 'the Attorney General had no role in them'. No IG finding had been reported as of the sources found.

sub_claims.statement: Bondi held Trump Media (DJT) stock as AG and sold it on 'Liberation Day'.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (her own periodic transaction report, disclosed May 14, 2025). It shows a sale of $1M-$5M of TMTG shares plus $250K-$500K of warrants on Apr 2, 2025, the day of the tariff announcement (Bloomberg Law gives a combined $1M-$5.5M). Her ethics agreement required her to sell the TMTG stake within 90 days of confirmation, and she says the shares were pay for consulting tied to DWAC, so the sale itself was mandated; the question raised is its timing. Rep. Raskin asked the DOJ IG to investigate (May 20, 2025). Mother Jones and Accountable.US had earlier flagged that Bondi, Patel and McMahon held TMTG shares or board ties when appointed. A sale before a market drop is not proof of insider trading. The holding itself was an interest in the president's company, held while she led the agency with jurisdiction over matters touching it. Trump fired Bondi as AG on Apr 2, 2026 and named Blanche acting AG (CBS, CNN via KVIA); no outcome of the Raskin IG referral was found.

sub_claims.statement: Todd Blanche held crypto when he signed the Apr 7, 2025 memo disbanding NCET.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (OGE 278 filings via ProPublica; Jan 28, 2026 letter from six Democratic senators). Blanche held roughly $159K-$485K in crypto assets (bitcoin, ether, solana); outlets give slightly different ranges. His ethics agreement required divestment within 90 days of confirmation. The 'Ending Regulation by Prosecution' memo came on Apr 7, 2025, and the divestment took place May 31-June 3, 2025. Per the Daily Beast's reading of his June 2025 ethics filing, the holdings 'were gifted in their entirety to my grandchild and adult children' rather than sold; experts say the narrow family exception may make that technically permissible. ProPublica's range is $158K-$470K and the Senate letter's $159K-$485K. Former federal ethics officials told ProPublica the memo likely breached 18 U.S.C. 208 and his agreement. The senators asked whether he had a 208(b)(1) waiver; no waiver has been published, and no official finding was found. The memo benefited the crypto sector as a class, not a former client. Blanche became acting AG when Trump fired Bondi on Apr 2, 2026 (CBS, Al Jazeera); we did not establish who holds the post as of Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Paul Atkins's Patomak clients and crypto holdings, and his recusal terms at the SEC.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (OGE ethics agreement and disclosure, Mar 2025). Patomak Global Partners advised banks, exchanges and DeFi firms. Patomak is listed as a creditor in the FTX bankruptcy for a Jan 2022 board-advisory agreement. Atkins disclosed up to ~$6M of crypto-related assets: equity in Anchorage Digital, Securitize call options plus a board seat (resigned Feb 2025), and a stake in the Off the Chain Capital fund. Reported ranges differ between outlets (Fortune/The Block vs others; see C54), so treat exact figures as ranges. He agreed to divest Patomak and Securitize options and to a one-year bar on specific-party matters involving Patomak clients and Securitize. He certified compliance to OGE on Jul 18, 2025. Senate Banking Democrats questioned the 140 divestitures and asked who bought Patomak; no buyer is public in what we found (audit re-check, Nov 2026: still none). The only public change is Patomak's Apr 22, 2025 announcement of a new supervisory board chaired by former SEC chair Richard Breeden (with ex-Fed vice chair Randal Quarles) and a seven-partner executive committee; it does not say who acquired Atkins's interest. Whether the partners bought it is unverified. The recusal does not cover industry-wide rulemaking, which is how most SEC crypto relief was delivered (see C23/C43).

sub_claims.statement: Atkins's former holding Securitize went public through a SPAC sponsored by the Lutnick family's Cantor Fitzgerald, with an SEC sign-off.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: the pieces are documented, the conflict link is inferred. Securitize, where Atkins held options and a board seat until Feb 2025, agreed in Oct 2025 to merge with Cantor Equity Partners II, a SPAC sponsored by a Cantor Fitzgerald affiliate. Cantor is now controlled by trusts for Howard Lutnick's children (see C35). The SEC declared the Form S-4 effective on June 5, 2026, with a shareholder vote set for June 29, 2026. Atkins's one-year Securitize bar would have lapsed around Feb 2026, and S-4 effectiveness is normally a staff action under delegated authority. No source asserts that Atkins took part or that anything improper happened. This is our cross-reference of three separately reported facts: an SEC chair's ex-holding, a Commerce secretary's family firm and an SEC approval. The merger closed on Jul 1, 2026 and Securitize began trading on the NYSE as SECZ on Jul 2, 2026, with about $400M of gross proceeds including a ~$197M PIPE (company release; Hughes Hubbard). Whether Atkins formally recused from the S-4 remains unknown.

sub_claims.statement: Mike Selig's former law-firm clients sit on the side of prediction-market fights his CFTC is now waging.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented links (OGE agreement; Intercept; InGame), with the benefit-to-client step inferred. As a Willkie Farr partner (2022-25), Selig represented dozens of crypto clients, including eToro, Paradigm and Alluvial Finance (Alluvial met his SEC Crypto Task Force staff). He co-signed a July 2024 Paradigm letter urging the CFTC to permit Kalshi's political event contracts, and Paradigm invested in Kalshi in June 2025. Zeteo reports that Willkie represents Polymarket. As CFTC chair he filed a Feb 17, 2026 amicus brief asserting exclusive federal jurisdiction over event contracts and sued AZ, CT and IL (Apr 2, 2026) and more states (see C25/C38). Those actions benefit Kalshi and Polymarket, where Don Jr. is an adviser and 1789 Capital an investor. His recusal covers only specific-party matters involving Willkie or former clients for one year, so policy-wide actions fall outside it. No source alleges a breach.

sub_claims.statement: Brian Quintenz (Kalshi board, a16z) was nominated to chair the CFTC.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. Quintenz was a Kalshi board member and a16z crypto's policy head. He pledged to leave Kalshi's board if confirmed. The White House withdrew the nomination on Sep 30, 2025, after the Winklevoss twins opposed him; texts he released show Tyler Winklevoss raising Gemini's CFTC case. He never took office, so he made no decisions. The episode matters because the replacement, Selig, later joined Gemini's motion to vacate its CFTC judgment (C52), and Gemini's founders gave about $10M in BTC to MAGA Inc. 23 days later.

sub_claims.statement: Comptroller Jonathan Gould (ex-Bitfury) approved charters including World Liberty's.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented background and approvals; no prior-client benefit found. Gould was OCC chief counsel (2018-21), then Bitfury's chief legal officer (to Sep 2022), then a Jones Day partner. As Comptroller he oversaw conditional trust charters for Coinbase, Ripple, BitGo, Circle, Fidelity Digital Assets, Paxos and Crypto.com, and preliminary approval of World Liberty Trust Co. on Aug 14, 2026 (C12). He has denied acting as a 'Trump fixer'. We found no Bitfury application before the OCC, and no OGE disclosure detail on any retained Bitfury interest. No waiver or cooling-off record was found (as C54 also notes).

sub_claims.statement: Peter Navarro, a friend of Don Jr., initiated the Pentagon's $620M loan to 1789-backed Vulcan Elements.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (ProPublica, May 28, 2026, with DoD records and interviews; follow-up letters from lawmakers). Navarro is described as a friend of Don Jr. Don Jr. is among the people Navarro dedicated his latest book to, and lawmakers note that Don Jr. visited Navarro in prison. Navarro initiated the OSC loan request, and an unnamed Pentagon official said it was the only deal initiated by a top presidential aide. 1789 Capital invested in Vulcan in its Aug 2025 Series A, and the $1.4B package was announced on Nov 3, 2025. No financial interest of Navarro's in Vulcan is reported. 1789 and the Pentagon deny any role or influence, and Navarro calls the reporting 'fake news'.

sub_claims.statement: Commerce (Lutnick) put CHIPS money and equity into the same Vulcan package.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. The Nov 3, 2025 package included $50M of CHIPS incentives from Commerce (a preliminary, non-binding LOI) and reportedly a Commerce equity position. Outlets differ on whether these are one $50M or two, and Lutnick publicly promoted the deal. That puts both Lutnick's department and Hegseth's OSC in the 1789-backed company's financing. For Cantor/Lutnick-family links to other minerals beneficiaries see C60. No reporting has Lutnick personally tied to Vulcan.

sub_claims.statement: Pentagon investment leadership comes from Deputy Secretary Feinberg's former firm, Cerberus, and Cerberus-linked firms received DoD work.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the appointments and contracts; any steering is unverified. OSC Director David Lorch (since Nov 2025, also senior adviser to Feinberg) was a Cerberus managing director (official DoD bio). George Kollitides, a former Cerberus managing director under Feinberg and a former partner at Alvarez & Marsal Capital, heads the Economic Defense Unit (EDU, 'Deal Team Six'), which runs the BOND initiative; he does not run OSC (C74). He agreed to join the board of D. Boral Acquisition I before his Feb 4, 2026 appointment and joined six days after it (Bloomberg Government), and resigned from it 'for personal reasons' effective Sep 23, 2026 (8-K, per C74). On that board he sat from about Feb 10 to Sep 23, 2026 with Kevin McGurn, CEO of the Trump sons' New America Acquisition I and interim TMTG CEO (Bloomberg Government, per C74): a documented shared board seat, not evidence of any transaction. Alvarez & Marsal Federal received no-bid DoD contracts worth up to about $350M ($67.6M in Dec 2025; $281.1M in Jun 2026; about $31M paid). ProPublica did not establish that Kollitides selected the firm. Feinberg's ethics agreement let him place Cerberus interests in trusts for his adult children and keep a Cerberus administrative-services contract. Warren says at least four Cerberus-related firms won Golden Dome contracts. DoD says affiliations play no role in funding decisions.

sub_claims.statement: Scott Bessent: late divestment of China-exposed farmland, and an Argentina rescue that benefited a friend's fund.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the farmland, single-source and secondary for the Citrone link. OGE told Senate Finance that Bessent had missed his Apr 28, 2025 divestment deadline. About $25M of North Dakota farmland remained, a crop roughly 70% exported to China, while he led China trade talks. He said in Oct 2025 that he had divested it. On Argentina, Mother Jones and Popular Information reported that Rob Citrone of Discovery Capital, a friend and former Soros colleague of Bessent, held large Argentine positions and bought more bonds days before Treasury's $20B swap-line announcement (Sep-Oct 2025). Argentine press reported that he lobbied Bessent; the NYT said his role was unclear. Bessent denies that the swap was a gift to investors and says Treasury profited. Citrone is a personal friend, not a former client of Bessent's in office.

sub_claims.statement: Kash Patel was a Trump Media director who received a stock award just before becoming FBI director.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (SEC Form 4). TMTG granted Patel 25,946 restricted shares on Jan 28, 2025, worth about $779K-$840K. Patel told senators he did not and would not accept them and had no stake. Mother Jones reported that he earned $120K a year as a TMTG consultant from 2022, and the award was absent from his disclosure. We found no FBI decision benefiting TMTG. This records a tie, not a decision.

sub_claims.statement: Michael Kratsios (OSTP) held, and may still hold, Scale AI stock.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: the earlier holding is documented; current status is unverified; no decision found. ProPublica's disclosure tracker lists Scale AI Class B shares worth $1M-$5M (from an earlier filing). Kratsios was a Scale managing director from 2021 to Jan 2024, and his 2026 annual OGE 278 was certified compliant. Sen. Cantwell's questions concerned Scale labour complaints. We found no specific OSTP decision benefiting Scale. Audit re-check (Nov 2026): no source reports whether he sold or kept the shares after Meta bought 49% of Scale (Jun 12, 2025, ~$14.3B). A search-result excerpt of his 2026 annual 278e (e-signed Jun 10, 2026) shows a US bank cash account of $5M-$25M and small ETF holdings; the excerpt is partial, so we cannot tell whether Scale shares are still listed. A cash-out in the Meta transaction is possible but is our own inference; OGE and ProPublica pages could not be fetched here.

sub_claims.statement: Steve Witkoff's Gulf counterparties include Qatar's QIA, which bought his Park Lane hotel.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented; already established in C14/C53. QIA paid about $623M for the Park Lane in Aug 2023, buying from a Witkoff-Mubadala joint venture. Aryam (Tahnoon) bought 49% of WLF. Witkoff negotiates with Qatar and the UAE as envoy. No source shows a specific envoy decision benefiting these counterparties.

sub_claims.statement: Tom Barrack kept financial ties to TI Capital while pushing its role in the Iraq-Syria pipeline.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (Reuters investigation, Oct 9, 2026, seen only via syndication and Al-Monitor). Barrack and Ziad Ghandour set up a $250M investment venture in 2020, and Barrack disclosed a paid consulting role with it in 2024. As ambassador to Turkey and Syria envoy, he reportedly pressed Iraqi and Syrian officials to include TI Capital in the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline. In July 2026 Iraq and Syria signed MoUs with a consortium of TI Capital, Chevron and Qatar's UCC Holding (project cost $15B+). OGE had no waiver on file. Reuters found no evidence that Barrack profits from the pipeline. State says he has 'no affiliation with, role in, or financial interest in' the project and is ethics-compliant.

sub_claims.statement: Massad Boulos (Africa adviser) mediated a DRC minerals-for-security deal.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented role; no personal benefit found. Boulos, whose son is married to Tiffany Trump, ran SCOA Nigeria (Fadoul Group), and his business scale is disputed (NYT). He mediated the June 27, 2025 DRC-Rwanda peace and minerals framework. KoBold Metals credited him for helping its Manono lithium deal. Africa Confidential (single-source) calls Boulos and Gentry Beach, a longtime Don Jr. friend, 'prime movers' in the talks. Per the WSJ (single-source, relayed; see C75), Don Jr.'s lawyer sent Beach a cease-and-desist in Aug 2025 telling him to stop presenting himself as Don Jr.'s business partner; Beach denies receiving it. C75 found no Boulos or Trump-family financial stake in any DRC asset awarded under the framework (Chemaf to Virtus, Manono to KoBold, the Glencore stake MOU to Orion CMC), and Beach's Rubaya bid had not closed as of Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Charles Kushner (ambassador to France) made decisions benefiting prior business ties.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: none found. He was confirmed 51-45 in May 2025, after a 2020 pardon. Coverage is about diplomatic rows (summoned by France and absent). We found no reporting of a decision tied to Kushner Companies or Gulf money. Gulf money in the family runs through Jared's Affinity (C15). One dossier site's claims about his ethics agreement could not be verified and are omitted.

corrections: The brief calls the jet memo 'Bondi's legal memo'. It was reportedly drafted by OLC and signed by Bondi; it remains unreleased.
Bondi's personal pay from the Qatar contract is not on record. The $115K/month went to Ballard Partners.
Reported Atkins holding ranges differ between outlets (Securitize options $250K-$500K per Fortune/The Block vs larger figures elsewhere, incl. C54). Treat them as ranges.
Quintenz was never confirmed, so he made no decisions as an official.
Blanche did not sell all his crypto: his June 2025 filing (as reported) says the holdings were gifted to his grandchild and adult children, May 31-June 3, 2025.
Kollitides heads the Economic Defense Unit (which runs BOND), not OSC; he resigned from the D. Boral Acquisition I board effective Sep 23, 2026 (C74).
Blanche became acting AG on Apr 2, 2026 when Bondi was fired; earlier text said he 'succeeded Bondi as AG'.
The Securitize-CEPT merger closed on Jul 1, 2026 (NYSE: SECZ from Jul 2).
denials_and_context: DOJ: Bondi consulted career ethics officials who found no recusal was needed on the jet, and 'the Attorney General had no role' in the brother's cases.
The SEC says Atkins complies with his ethics agreement, and he certified compliance with OGE on Jul 18, 2025.
Patel says he never accepted TMTG compensation as a director.
1789 Capital and the Pentagon deny any role or influence in the Vulcan loan, and Navarro calls the reporting 'fake news'.
Bessent says the Argentina swap was not a bailout and that Treasury profited.
State Department: Barrack has no role or financial interest in the pipeline and is certified ethics-compliant.
Gould denies receiving any presidential direction on WLF's charter.
Most crypto relief came through industry-wide policy, which the standard one-year recusals do not cover. This is lawful, but it means recusal terms do not address the main channel of benefit.
Bondi's TMTG sale was required by her ethics agreement (divest within 90 days of confirmation); critics question only the timing.

Research note (updated by audit): Patomak's buyer is still not public, Kratsios's post-Meta Scale status is unverified, and Gentry Beach's role is covered in C75. govexec.com, OGE and ProPublica's tracker could not be fetched directly.
